title: Ismail and Ibrahim: A Conversation Between Colleagues
script: Bayu: [thoughtful] Citra, I've been chewing on the story of Ibrahim and Ismail all week, specifically the part everyone rushes past to get to the ram.
Citra: The dream itself, you mean, where Ibrahim sees himself sacrificing his son and takes it as instruction from Allah?
Bayu: [carefully] Right, and what gets skipped is that he actually tells Ismail about the dream beforehand, rather than simply acting on it unilaterally.
Citra: That detail matters more than people give it credit for. He's not imposing a decision; he's disclosing one, and asking his son's view of it.
Bayu: [reflective] And Ismail's answer is startling for someone reportedly still a boy: do what you've been commanded, you'll find me patient, if Allah wills it.
Citra: No negotiation, no bargaining for his life, and crucially, no performance of bravado either. It's a strangely composed response for the situation.
Bayu: [honestly] I think what unsettles modern readers isn't the obedience itself, but how calmly it's rendered, as though panic would somehow have been the more honest reaction.
Citra: Maybe, but consider what's actually being tested here. It isn't merely Ibrahim's willingness to obey; it's whether love for his son had quietly displaced everything else in his priorities.
Bayu: [gently] Which reframes the whole episode for me. This isn't a story about a father's cruelty narrowly avoided; it's about a devotion that had to prove it hadn't become idolatry in disguise.
Citra: And then the substitution arrives at the very last instant, a ram provided in Ismail's place, once the intention itself had already been fully carried out internally.
Bayu: [calmly] So the sacrifice, in some sense, had already happened before the knife ever moved, in the willingness rather than the outcome.
Citra: Exactly, and that's why the ritual gets repeated every year afterward, not to commemorate a killing that occurred, but a surrender that did.
Bayu: [encouraging] It reframes how I think about my own attachments, honestly, the quiet ways love for something good can slowly crowd out everything it was supposed to serve.
Citra: That's precisely why this story refuses to age, I think. It isn't really about a knife at all. It's about what we'd actually be willing to relinquish.

quiz.question: What does Ibrahim do before acting on his dream?
options: He consults his advisors
He keeps it entirely secret
He asks Allah for a different dream
He tells Ismail about the dream and asks his view
quiz.explanation: Ibrahim tells Ismail about the dream beforehand rather than simply acting on it unilaterally, and asks his son's view.

quiz.question: How does Ismail respond to learning of the dream?
options: He begs for his life
He tells his father to do what he's been commanded and says he'll find him patient
He runs away
He questions whether the dream was real
quiz.explanation: Ismail says to do what has been commanded, and that Ibrahim will find him patient, if Allah wills it.

quiz.question: According to Citra, what is actually being tested in the episode?
options: Ismail's physical strength
Whether love for his son had displaced everything else in Ibrahim's priorities
Ibrahim's skill with a knife
The family's wealth
quiz.explanation: Citra suggests the test is whether love for his son had quietly displaced everything else in Ibrahim's priorities.

quiz.question: When did Bayu suggest the sacrifice had effectively already happened?
options: Only after the ram appeared
Years before the dream
It never actually happened
In the willingness itself, before the knife ever moved
quiz.explanation: Bayu says the sacrifice had already happened before the knife moved, in the willingness rather than the outcome.

quiz.question: What does Citra say the annual ritual actually commemorates?
options: A surrender that occurred, not a killing
A killing that occurred
Ismail's bravery alone
The ram's sacrifice specifically
quiz.explanation: Citra says the ritual is repeated not to commemorate a killing that occurred, but a surrender that did.

quiz.question: Which reported detail shapes the colleagues' emphasis on consultation?
options: He leaves his mission without explicit permission after frustration.
They seek food, reassurance, and certainty about Isa's truthfulness.
Ibrahim tells Ismail the dream and asks for his response.
Prudent planning operates with faith rather than against it.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the source-aware distinction: Ibrahim tells Ismail the dream and asks for his response.

quiz.question: How do the speakers interpret Ismail's answer without inventing hidden speech?
options: It affirms Allah and admits wrongdoing without self-defence.
He tests whether it reflects faith rather than appetite alone.
They emphasise willing obedience expressed in the reported reply.
A spider's web and a nearby dove make the entrance appear undisturbed.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the source-aware distinction: They emphasise willing obedience expressed in the reported reply.

quiz.question: What deeper test do they infer beyond the physical act?
options: Attachment to a beloved son must not displace devotion to Allah.
The sequence links truthful acknowledgment with deliverance from distress.
Greater evidence creates greater responsibility for those receiving it.
It redirects attention to Allah without denying the real danger.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the source-aware distinction: Attachment to a beloved son must not displace devotion to Allah.

quiz.question: Why is the substitution read as following an inward surrender?
options: Others using Yunus's invocation in anguish will also be answered.
It should become a sign, provision, and recurring occasion.
Sincere believers can still face capture, exile, or death.
Willingness is already established before the sacrifice is prevented.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the source-aware distinction: Willingness is already established before the sacrifice is prevented.

quiz.question: What cautious modern implication do the colleagues draw?
options: Accountability begins with specific admission rather than a polished excuse.
Vivid certainty increases accountability rather than merely providing comfort.
Good attachments should be examined when they crowd out higher obligations.
Composure can rest on Allah without certainty about the outcome.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the source-aware distinction: Good attachments should be examined when they crowd out higher obligations.
